changed: finalized each test log before persisting its terminal result, including cancellation, timeout, and spawn failures
serialized writes, rotation, and close; prevented late output from reopening completed logs
pruned obsolete UUID log files and rotated copies after completion, recovery, and project removal while preserving retained and active output
preserved prune requests arriving during scan completion and kept slow cleanup independent of queue progress
awaited queued cancellation through shared services and transports, observed background finalization failures, and completed shutdown cleanup even when another cancellation failed
summary: Completed jobs release their log handles and writer entries without waiting for controller shutdown. Write or close errors are reported and cannot turn a failed verification into a passed run.

File retention follows the existing fifty-completed-runs-per-project history policy, including interrupted-run recovery. Cleanup streams directory entries, avoids symlinks and unrelated names, and does not delete active or queued output.

Review follow-up fixed one scan-completion race from the recovered Claude analysis and both published Kimi findings. Codex reported no additional actionable findings; both inline threads were resolved before merge. Suppressing known logging failures during shutdown was rejected because it would hide an operational error.
title: Closed completed test logs and aligned file retention with run history
validation: pnpm check passed ESLint, TypeScript, and 188 tests in 35 files on final PR head 1bea74e5a7824c7cef251596a92fd0e11e428ffc.
pnpm build completed the static Next.js export and bundled controller CLI; git diff --check passed.
Twelve real jobs in an isolated Linux fixture left zero open test-log descriptors after completion and retained their final output.

Regression fixtures cover all terminal paths, file rotation, history retention, recovery, project removal, symlink protection, delayed close, slow pruning, the microtask handoff race, asynchronous cancellation responses, and persistence failures during finalization and shutdown.
No CI checks were configured on the PR. No production service restart or browser QA was performed.
